name: Apollo GraphQL Studio
description: Apollo GraphOS Studio is a cloud platform for managing, observing, and delivering GraphQL APIs.
agentUseSummary: Connect a dedicated customer-owned graph-scoped Consumer or Observer API key. Agents can read only current OCI graph-artifact metadata and one exact launch status through fixed Platform API documents. Schemas, operations, telemetry, mutations, administration, broad credentials, and raw GraphQL remain blocked.

credentialRequirements.name: APOLLO_GRAPHOS_API_KEY
credentialRequirements.label: Customer-owned graph API key
credentialRequirements.helpText: Use a dedicated graph-scoped Consumer or Observer key, never a personal or organization-wide key. Relay encrypts its copy; delete the key in GraphOS Studio after disconnect.

credentialRequirements.name: APOLLO_GRAPH_ID
credentialRequirements.label: Graph ID
credentialRequirements.helpText: The exact GraphOS graph ID this connection may inspect.

credentialRequirements.name: APOLLO_GRAPH_VARIANT
credentialRequirements.label: Graph variant
credentialRequirements.helpText: The exact GraphOS variant, such as current, this connection may inspect.

capabilities.label: Read graph artifact metadata
capabilities.description: Read only current OCI artifact location and digest metadata for the configured graph variant.

capabilities.label: Read launch status
capabilities.description: Read only the status of one exact launch for the configured graph variant.

allowed.label: Read graph artifact metadata
allowed.description: Read the current OCI graph-artifact tag and digest metadata for the configured graph and variant through two fixed Platform API queries.

allowed.label: Read launch status
allowed.description: Read the status of one exact launch identifier for the configured graph and variant through one fixed Platform API query.

blocked.label: Block graph content and telemetry
blocked.description: Schemas, SDL, subgraphs, operations, traces, metrics, insights, proposals, persisted queries, graph configuration, and organization data are unavailable.

blocked.label: Block mutations and administration
blocked.description: Schema publishing and checks, graph and variant changes, integration changes, API-key management, persisted-query changes, proposals, router settings, telemetry settings, and all other mutations are unavailable.

blocked.label: Block raw access and broad credentials
blocked.description: Arbitrary GraphQL, introspection, fragments, user-supplied variables, batching, pagination, retries, redirects, personal keys, organization keys, operator keys, subgraph keys, cookies, and browser sessions are unavailable.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Two fixed metadata reads run automatically; graph content, telemetry, mutations, administration, broad credentials, and raw GraphQL remain blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: The same two fixed reads run without per-action approval; fixed documents, exact graph binding, response reduction, audits, and provider limits still apply.

runtimeSupport.description: Relay mounts two fixed bounded metadata reads while Railway alone holds the graph key and exact graph/variant binding.
Relay mounts two fixed bounded metadata reads while Railway alone holds the graph key and exact graph/variant binding.

providerSetup.blocker: A representative GraphOS organization, dedicated least-privilege graph key, current plan-role confirmation, current terms/privacy review, staging credential entry, live response validation, and provider-side key lifecycle testing remain for separate authorized tasks.
providerSetup.nextAction: An authorized provider task must create a dedicated Consumer or Observer graph key for a test graph, store the key and exact graph/variant in Railway staging, then validate only the fixed documents, response reduction, 256 KiB limit, no retry or pagination, encrypted-copy deletion, provider-side key deletion, and post-deletion denial.

evidence.supports: Apollo documents the GraphOS Platform GraphQL API endpoint, x-api-key authentication, supported read operations and mutations, and the broader authority that Relay must narrow.
Apollo documents graph API keys, graph-level roles, secret handling, key deletion, and the broader cross-graph authority of personal keys, which Relay prohibits.
Apollo publishes the exact graph, variant, launch and status Platform API query shape used by the fixed launch-status action.
Apollo publishes the exact graphArtifactTagLocation and graphArtifactByTag query shapes used by the bounded artifact-metadata action.
Apollo documents Platform API limits; Relay performs no automatic retry or pagination and enforces a smaller local response bound.
